# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 66 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 66 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_066_page_001.jpg

---

## Council Notes

This chapter is deeply personal: the Shepherd identifies Hermas himself as having been "delivered to the angel of punishment." The reason given is not Hermas's own direct sin but his failure to govern his household (*oikos*), which has committed "great and terrible iniquities." The household-head bears responsibility for his family's moral state — a standard ancient Roman (and Jewish) concept.

The statement "your sins are the sins of those of your household" (*hai hamartiai tōn sōn oikeion sai eisin*) has parallels in Achan's household guilt (Josh 7) and the Pauline household codes. Hermas's family appears elsewhere in the Shepherd as a source of grief and difficulty.

The answer to Hermas's question in 66:4 — "can they be saved?" — is "yes, but slowly." The complete term of punishment must be served. This is Hermas's closest approach to a purgatorial doctrine.

EMET's "be subdued" and LOGOS's "be brought low" both render *tapeinōthē* (be humbled/brought low). SOPHIA uses "be brought low" — the same root as *tapeinōsis* (humility) throughout the Shepherd.

---

## Similitude 6, Part 4 — Hermas and the Angel of Punishment

**66:1** "Lord," I asked, "why has this angel of punishment been assigned to me rather than the angel of righteousness?" "Because," he said, "you have sinned greatly and have been delivered to this angel for chastisement, so that he may afflict you and humble you, until you learn what you need to learn."

**66:2** "I do not know, lord," I said, "what great sin I have committed." "Your sins are many," he said, "but not so great that you had to be delivered to this angel permanently. But your household has committed great and terrible iniquities against the Lord, and for this reason you were delivered to this angel."

**66:3** "But I have not sinned," I said. "I have not sinned against the Lord." "Yes you have," he said. "For the sins of those in your household are your sins. You did not take care of your own household, but allowed it to fall into complete corruption. Therefore you share in their sins."

**66:4** "Since I have heard these things, lord, and know they are true," I said, "tell me this as well: if those who have been tormented in this way are able to repent, will they be saved?" "They can repent," he said, "but they cannot be saved quickly. The one who has been delivered to this angel must complete his torments and be brought low, and complete the full term of his punishment — and only then may he be saved."

---

*SOPHIA represents the consensus rendering of EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA, with rulings recorded in the Disagreement Log.*
